assigned passages. start lesson 1 all ten lessons final quiz and certificate back to all manuals · search learning resources start with bookshare in a desktop browser. device-specific apps may use different labels. membership eligibility and available access must be confirmed with bookshare; this guide does not promise free access for every reader. documentation checked september 17, 2026. these instructions have not been tested here with the actual windows assistive software or a signed-in reading-service account. control names can vary by version. follow the label you hear rather than counting tab presses. first-time learner: how to follow a task before you begin reading-service terms explained 1. prepare the correct membership 2. search for the correct book and edition 3. open, play, and navigate bookshare reader on the web 4. find assigned reading and mark your place 5. choose a reading device 6. build a recovery routine sign in and check whether your account can read bookshare reader web shortcuts and study notes use bookshare reader on a phone or tablet iphone and android: focus, activate, and enter text check offline readiness and recover a missing passage keyboard and control reference independent practice related learning practice this topic in mission control first-time learner: how to follow a task read the task title and its starting location before pressing anything. a keyboard command acts on the active application and focused control. merely having these instructions visible does not make the other application active. keep these instructions available. open the application separately. on windows, hold alt, tap tab to choose its window, and release alt. check the window title before continuing. focus is the place receiving your next keystroke. a screen reader announces its name and role; a visible border or highlight may mark it. tab selects the next keyboard-accessible control. shift+tab reverses that movement. neither command means “activate.” at a button or link, press enter to activate. a checkbox is an on/off choice: space changes it. listen for checked or not checked. in an open menu, use arrows to select an item, then enter. escape usually closes that menu; it does not universally return to the previous page. at a text field, enter only the requested information. ctrl+a selects all text in that field ; typing then replaces it. confirm focus before doing this. use left and right to review a small correction, or backspace to remove the character before the cursor. after opening a dialog, listen to its title, read its instructions, and tab through its controls. use cancel if you are unsure. do not repeatedly activate a button while a page or file is loading. at the result checkpoint, stop. say what changed. if the result is different, use that task’s recovery paragraph before attempting the next task. with a screen reader, arrow-key reading and text editing can use different modes. if letters become navigation commands instead of text, confirm you reached an editable field and consult your reader’s forms/focus-mode instructions in the screen readers manual . do not turn the reader off to solve an unidentified focus problem. when a task says to locate a named control, start with tab or shift+tab and listen to each complete label and role. tab skips ordinary paragraphs. if the page itself needs to be read, use your screen reader’s reading commands. if you pass the same controls twice without finding the requested one, stop and check the application, page, account, and open dialogs. a fixed number of tab presses is unreliable because layouts change. recording progress: write down the task, your starting location, the result, and one step to practice again. these activities are optional and repeatable; they are not a sequence of locked lessons. before you begin choose one practice task at a time. have your usual accessibility tools running and a way to record which steps helped. use a familiar, non-sensitive document or book for the first exercise. keyboard directions a plus sign means hold the first key while tapping the final key, then release both. for three-key combinations, hold both modifiers while tapping the last key. do not type the plus sign. “then” means release the first command before pressing the next key. tab moves forward through controls; shift+tab moves backward. enter activates a focused link or button; space commonly operates buttons and checkboxes. arrow keys move within menus and lists. pause after each step to check where focus went. for screen-reader reading and interaction modes, see the screen readers manual . phone gestures are covered in the iphone and ipad voiceover and android talkback manuals. reading-service terms explained membership and sign-in membership determines access. signing in proves which account is using the service. installing an app by itself does not establish membership. catalog and bookshelf the catalog is the collection you can search. your bookshelf or reading list is a smaller set selected for your use. a title in a list is not necessarily downloaded to your device. edition and format an edition is a particular published version. a format is how the content is delivered. match the assigned title, author, and edition before relying on its page numbering. playback position, bookmark, and note playback position is where reading currently is. a bookmark marks a place to revisit. a note records your own words. stopping at a passage does not automatically create a meaningful study note. download and synchronization a download stores content on one device. synchronization exchanges supported account information while connected. neither guarantees that a second device has the full book stored for offline use. keep a simple reading record: book title, edition, chapter or page, device, and one sentence about where to resume. it gives you a way to recover even when an app does not reopen at the expected position. 1. prepare the correct membership what you will learn: separate individual reading access from organizational administration. exactly how to do it if a school or organization already provides your access, ask for its member sign-in instructions before making another account. for a new individual membership, open bookshare’s sign up page and choose the individual route. complete the required information. follow the confirmation and proof-of-disability process. review the current membership terms and any applicable fee or assistance before activation. what should happen: you know which account to use and whether its access is ready. if that does not happen: a created account is not necessarily an activated membership. check the outstanding requirements before troubleshooting the reader. practice: write down the account route and next required step, but do not put your password or disability paperwork in a practice worksheet. source: bookshare membership setup . 2. search for the correct book and edition start here: bookshare in a browser. have the title and author, and an isbn if your assignment specifies one. step-by-step instructions tab to the site’s book-search field. enter a distinctive title or author and activate search. an isbn can help identify a particular edition. read the results heading and count. move through the results using links or your screen reader’s page-reading commands, rather than assuming the first result is correct. open a likely result and review its title, author, description, and available publication information. compare those details with the assignment. if the edition is wrong, return to the results or perform a narrower search. record the correct title before opening the reader. if you are exploring rather than seeking an assignment, use the site’s browsing categories or explore options. treat recommendations as choices, not as required lesson order. check your result you can explain why the selected book matches your reading goal. if something goes wrong if there are no matches, check spelling and try fewer distinctive words. a book with the same short title may be by a different author. if required edition information is unclear, ask the instructor before starting page-specific work. try it yourself find one title by author and another by a distinctive title phrase. verify each author before reading. documentation: bookshare searching and exploring . 3. open, play, and navigate bookshare reader on the web start here: a book’s details page in your signed-in browser account, or a book assigned in your reading list. step-by-step instructions locate read now and activate it. wait for the reader to open. read the book title and identify the player controls before starting audio. use tab to locate play and activate it. listen to a short passage. return to the player’s pause or stop control before exploring other settings. open book navigation to inspect the chapter list. select the intended chapter, return to the text, and verify its heading or opening words. open settings and inspect its audio and display choices. change one preference at a time and compare the same paragraph after each change. if the player voice and your screen reader compete, pause book playback while you navigate controls. start it again after you have returned to the reading location. before leaving, record a chapter or page reference and create a bookmark if needed. reopen the book to check your return location instead of assuming it. check your result you can read a passage, stop playback, and intentionally choose a chapter. if something goes wrong if audio does not begin, first confirm the book has opened and the player is active. then check device volume and audio output. an account-access error needs account support, not a volume adjustment. try it yourself read one paragraph, stop, navigate to another chapter, then return to the original passage. documentation: bookshare reader web workflow . 4. find assigned reading and mark your place what you will learn: return to a useful passage. exactly how to do it with organizational member access, check assigned books or reading lists for the material provided to you. open the book with read now. locate the assigned chapter using book navigation. create a bookmark at a passage you want to revisit, then practice returning to it. what should happen: you can distinguish the assignment location from your position inside the book. if that does not happen: if a title is missing, confirm which member account received it. ask the assigning instructor to check the assignment rather than sharing account credentials. practice: choose a passage, record a short description, and use your bookmark to return to it. source: assignments and bookmarks . 5. choose a reading device what you will learn: match the reading tool to your access needs. exactly how to do it review bookshare’s supported reading tools. bookshare reader is available for browsers, ios, android, and alexa; partner tools provide other options. choose one tool and sign in through its documented bookshare connection. try a short book on that device before depending on it for a long assignment. what should happen: you have a workable reading method for your device. if that does not happen: do not assume all tools use identical controls or support every format. check the selected tool’s instructions. practice: compare listening, enlarged text, or braille according to your needs. explain which method you would choose for leisure versus study. source: supported reading tools . 6. build a recovery routine what you will learn: describe an access problem clearly. exactly how to do it separate sign-in trouble, missing book access, navigation trouble, and missing sound. write down the book title, device, reading tool, and exact error. do not include passwords. use the bookshare help and learning center for that specific problem. for an organizational account, involve the instructor who manages access. what should happen: your support request describes something another person can investigate. if that does not happen: avoid deleting a book, reinstalling the app, or creating duplicate accounts before identifying the problem. practice: pretend a book opens but has no sound. list what you would check before concluding that the book is unavailable. source: bookshare help . sign in and check whether your account can read start here: a browser at bookshare , with the account information supplied to you. if a school manages access, use its instructions first. step-by-step instructions locate the sign-in control with tab and activate it. read the form’s field labels. enter the account email or member username required by your route, then the password in its password field. activate the form’s sign-in button once and wait. check for an account page or a clear error before retrying. if the school supplied organizational membership, check for assigned books or reading lists. an adult’s administrative account and a learner’s reading account are not interchangeable. for new individual membership, follow the official sign-up process, including requested eligibility verification and any applicable membership requirement. a confirmation email alone may not mean all access steps are complete. open a book you are authorized to read and check whether read now is available. if access is restricted, note the displayed explanation and resolve account access before troubleshooting the player. on a shared device, finish using the account’s sign-out control. closing a tab is not the same as signing out. check your result you can identify the reading account and whether it has active access to a book. if something goes wrong use the site’s account-recovery process for forgotten credentials. if a school manages the account, ask its authorized staff which sign-in route to use rather than creating a duplicate account. try it yourself explain the difference between installing a reader, signing in, and having an active reading membership. documentation: bookshare membership setup · web reading access . bookshare reader web shortcuts and study notes these shortcuts are for bookshare reader on the website , with the reader active. they are not phone gestures or universal commands for partner reading apps. bookshare reader: windows and linux action keys contents alt+c add bookmark / list bookmarks alt+b / alt+shift+b add note alt+n start / stop reading alt+r / alt+shift+r go to page alt+p settings alt+t current location alt+w on mac, substitute control+option for alt. jaws may require its pass-through command, jaws key+3, before a reader shortcut. create and retrieve a note at the passage, activate note or the note shortcut. in add note, type your comment and choose save; cancel discards it. open book navigation, then bookmarks & notes, to revisit it. an edited note needs save again; delete removes it. source: bookshare web notes and shortcuts . practice with a useful study note choose a short passage and record its location on paper or in your ordinary notes app before trying the reader’s note feature. write one original question about that passage, save it in the reader, leave the passage, and use the saved item to return. check that both the question and the location are correct. if a shortcut performs a browser or screen-reader action, stop and use the labeled player control instead. confirm the active window and focused area before trying the shortcut again. use bookshare reader on a phone or tablet start here: an active membership, a connection, and the official bookshare reader app for your platform. see the separate gesture instructions below. step-by-step instructions use bookshare’s official reading-tools guidance to locate the appropriate app. in the app store, confirm the bookshare reader name and benetech developer before installing. open the app and sign in to the reading account. explore the app’s labeled tabs and identify your books or reading lists. select the intended title. verify the title and author before choosing a reading or download action. on the documented iphone app, selecting a book opens more information, where read now and download choices are available. other versions and android may arrange those controls differently: use their spoken labels. open the book and locate playback controls. start a brief passage, then pause before opening settings. change a single reading preference and return to the same passage to compare. for offline reading, complete the download on this device while connected. check the download’s status and open the book before leaving your connection. to continue on a second device, sign in to the same account and open the same book while connected. verify the returned passage. download separately on that device if you need offline access there. check your result you can identify the book, operate playback, and distinguish account progress from a downloaded local copy. if something goes wrong if a listed book will not play offline, reconnect and inspect its download status. do not remove the app as a first troubleshooting step: you may remove local downloads or unsynchronized work. try it yourself download a short authorized book, record a passage, and test that book on the same device without a connection when it is convenient to do so. documentation: supported bookshare reading tools · official iphone app and release details · official android app . iphone and android: focus, activate, and enter text iphone or ipad with voiceover swipe right with one finger to the next item; swipe left to the previous item. a one-finger double-tap activates the selected item. at a text field, select it and double-tap to edit. with standard typing, select a keyboard key then double-tap; touch typing instead enters the selected key when you lift your finger. android with talkback swipe right or left with one finger to move focus. double-tap to activate. use two fingers to scroll. keyboard entry depends on the keyboard and typing settings; on gboard, locate a key by touch and lift to enter it. use this routine with the reading app before activating anything, hear its full label. the book title, a download control, and the play control perform different actions. activate once, wait, and identify the new screen. an app can open an account page or download details rather than immediately playing. during book narration, pause the player before exploring unfamiliar controls so their labels are easier to hear. if the expected item is missing, check whether a dialog, keyboard, or menu is still open. follow the device’s back or dismissal behavior and identify where you land. if voiceover or talkback is off, ordinary touch interaction applies: tap the labeled control to activate it. these touch directions do not define external-keyboard shortcuts. customized gestures may differ; use your device’s screen-reader help if the standard gesture does something else. documentation: apple voiceover operation , voiceover typing , talkback gestures , and talkback typing . continue with the full voiceover manual or talkback manual for device-level practice. check offline readiness and recover a missing passage start here: the installed reading app on the exact device you will use away from the internet. browser access alone is not proof of offline readiness. step-by-step instructions while connected, select the intended book and complete the app’s download procedure. check the status until it indicates completion; a title appearing on a shelf is not sufficient. open the downloaded book and read a short passage. note its title, edition, chapter, and page or section. at a convenient time when disconnecting will not interrupt another task, temporarily disconnect that device and test the same book. confirm that you can start playback and navigate to a second passage. reconnect afterward. if offline playback failed, check storage, download status, and app-specific help while connected. do not erase other people’s files to free space. when continuing elsewhere, open the same account and book edition, then compare the current passage with your written location. use navigation or a bookmark to recover if needed. before removing downloads or reinstalling an app, check whether important notes and progress are synchronized or recorded elsewhere. check your result you know whether this book on this device works offline and have a way to regain your place. if something goes wrong report the device, app/version, title, connection state, exact message, and last successful action. keep passwords and private account information out of support screenshots. try it yourself demonstrate offline reading for one downloaded title, reconnect, and return to your recorded passage. documentation: official reading-app guidance . keyboard and control reference desktop browser control routine purpose action move among links and buttons tab; shift+tab to go back activate the selected control enter, or space for a button begin reading find the player’s play control and activate it change chapter open book navigation and select the chapter adjust reading preferences open the reader’s settings these are navigation routines, not universal bookshare single-key shortcuts. confirm the focused control and pause narration while exploring. source: reader controls . independent practice choose any activity; there is no required order or passing score. identify your membership route and whether access is active. find a book by title and verify the author. find a chapter and summarize one paragraph. return to a marked passage. explain how a sign-in problem differs from a playback problem. after each task, record whether you completed it independently, needed a prompt, or want another attempt. repeat the difficult step instead of restarting everything. related learning for braille-device reading, continue with the brailliant bi x or victor reader stream 3 manual. compare the learning ally manual . this manual now has ten dedicated lessons, a final quiz, and a printable course-completion certificate. lesson completion is self-reported. back to all manuals · back to the beginning practice this topic in mission control choose command practice or choose topic missions , then select bookshare. these are simulated exercises; they do not operate the actual app or account. topic missions presents a troubleshooting problem. command practice explains and checks one keyboard action at a time. use settings to choose speech and sound feedback. escape returns to the topic list during a session. when a simulator prompt says protected practice, release the modifier before the final key as instructed. in the real application, use the held keyboard combination in this manual. completing a simulation does not confirm that the real application received or performed a command. © 2026 creating a duplicate account when access is already provided. exactly how to do it ask whether access is through a school, a household, or an individual adult membership. for school access, use the school’s instructions. clever, classlink, or google sso accounts may require the school sign-in option rather than a manual username-and-password form. for new individual access, review current membership and eligibility requirements with learning ally before registering. what should happen: you know the correct sign-in method and outstanding membership steps. if that does not happen: if credentials appear correct but fail, check the sign-in route before repeatedly resetting the password. practice: explain which route you use without disclosing your password. source: learning ally membership and login help . 2. choose and open your reading app what you will learn: use the official application for your device. exactly how to do it open learning ally’s app page and choose the web reader or the download for your supported device. sign in with the reader’s approved access method. explore the bookshelf and navigation controls before opening an important assignment. what should happen: you can identify the account and reading environment you are using. if that does not happen: a school management screen and the student reading screen serve different purposes. ask the account administrator if you cannot reach the reading area. practice: find the bookshelf, the search function, and the way back to your current book. source: official learning ally apps . 3. search, verify, and add a book to your bookshelf start here: the signed-in learning ally reading app or browser reader. have the assigned title, author, and edition information. step-by-step instructions locate the app’s search or browse option through its labeled navigation. activate search and enter a distinctive title or author in the search field. submit the search once. read the result titles and inspect likely matches. compare author and edition with your assignment before adding a book. open the intended book’s details and use its add-to-bookshelf action. confirm the action’s result before returning to the bookshelf. on the bookshelf, locate the title you added and open it. identify whether it can be read now or whether the app is downloading content. if the assigned book is already on the shelf, open that matching edition instead of adding another similarly named title. record the selected edition and a chapter title for your first reading task. keep this record if your class uses printed page references. check your result the correct title is on your bookshelf and you know how to open it again. if something goes wrong if the title is missing, confirm the account and clear any bookshelf search/filter. a book added under another account will not necessarily appear here. ask the instructor about an unavailable edition instead of substituting silently. try it yourself find an assigned title and explain how its author and edition distinguish it from a similar result. documentation: learning ally app and bookshelf workflow . 4. start reading, choose a passage, and mark your place start here: an open book in the learning ally reader. keep its assigned passage or chapter written down. step-by-step instructions explore the player controls with tab on desktop, or screen-reader focus gestures on mobile. identify the labeled playback control before activating it. there is no single keyboard shortcut established here for all versions of the app. start a short passage and confirm that it is the intended book. pause playback before investigating navigation so the book narration does not compete with spoken control labels. open the available navigation control and inspect its chapter, section, or page options. choose the passage your edition supports. read its heading or opening words to confirm where you arrived. if using a page number, compare the book’s printed-page information with the app’s displayed location. do not assume an audio position or section count is the printed page number. locate the playback-speed control and make one small adjustment. replay a brief passage and choose the speed at which you can explain its meaning. use the player’s bookmark action at a useful study point. if a label or description is offered, make it meaningful, such as “chapter 2 — review question.” move to another passage, open the bookmarks list, and activate the saved item. verify the returned location against your written record. check your result you can deliberately reach a passage and use a saved marker to return to it. if something goes wrong if a control is absent, check that the book is open in the player rather than selected on the bookshelf. versions differ in available study controls. use a separate notes document for your explanation if the current reader does not expose a usable note field. try it yourself read one section, pause, summarize it in your own words, and return to one sentence supporting your summary. documentation: learning ally reading navigation · official android playback and study features . 5. prepare for reading away from the internet what you will learn: check that the book is actually downloaded. exactly how to do it while online in a supported app, add the title to the bookshelf and complete its download. open it once before leaving your connection. at a convenient time, test a short offline reading session. reconnect afterward. what should happen: you know whether that device and book are ready for offline use. if that does not happen: adding a title is not the same as completing its download. check the app and download state; do not assume the web reader behaves like an installed app. practice: prepare one book for a trip. record the device, title, and whether your offline test succeeded. source: offline reading guidance . 6. troubleshoot without losing your work what you will learn: keep useful evidence before changing the setup. exactly how to do it identify the problem: sign-in, missing title, sound, download, or reading position. record the app or browser, device, title, and any error text. for sign-in problems, confirm the school or individual route. for account questions, use learning ally’s help center or the school administrator. what should happen: you have a precise description and the right support route. if that does not happen: do not uninstall the app or remove downloads as a first step. first note any reading position or study work you need to keep. practice: describe a hypothetical problem in two sentences: what you tried and what happened instead. source: learning ally support . sign in through the correct school or individual route start here: your approved learning ally access information. ask whether access comes from your school or an individual membership before making a new account. step-by-step instructions open the official learning ally app page and choose the web reader or the appropriate installed app. for the browser reader, use read.learningally.org . at sign-in, inspect the available routes before typing. if your school uses clever, classlink, or google single sign-on, follow its school-login instructions. single sign-on means the school authenticates you through its own approved service. for a direct account, enter the supplied username and password in their labeled fields, then activate sign-in once. wait and read the resulting page or error. identify the learner’s bookshelf. an educator management account is not necessarily the same view as the learner’s reading app. for new household or adult access, follow learning ally’s membership and eligibility process. do not assume an app download has completed those steps. record the correct route in your private learning notes without recording the password. on a shared device, sign out when finished. check your result you reach the intended reader’s books using the appropriate account route. if something goes wrong if school sign-in fails, ask the school to verify access and the approved route. if a direct password is forgotten, use the service’s recovery option. repeatedly trying another person’s credentials is not a useful test. try it yourself explain which sign-in route you use and who can help with an account-access problem. documentation: learning ally account and school-login help · official reading apps . build a study routine with notes and bookmarks start here: a familiar passage in a book, with playback paused. have a separate notes document available as an alternative. step-by-step instructions record the title, edition, chapter, and page or section. this context makes the note useful even if another device opens at a different location. write a short summary or question in your own words. if the installed app provides an accessible note action, open it, enter the note in its labeled field, and activate its save/confirmation control. if the book and version provide text highlighting, select the intended text using that app’s supported selection method, then apply the available highlight action. do not assume every audiobook presents selectable full text. reopen the saved study item and read it. confirm it refers to the intended passage rather than relying on an icon or a changed color alone. if you plan to change devices, reconnect and allow supported study information to synchronize. check the same note or bookmark on the second device before relying on it. keep a short separate record of essential assignment locations. it is useful when the app cannot display a particular study feature or when you need to explain a problem to an instructor. check your result your study record contains both an idea and enough location information to find its source passage. if something goes wrong if a note disappears, check the book edition, account, device connection, and whether you actually saved it. do not uninstall the app or clear its storage while investigating unsynchronized work. try it yourself create one summary and one question, then return to their passages without listening from the beginning. documentation: learning ally study and synchronization features · learning ally android study tools . open and use learning ally on iphone, ipad, or android start here: an approved learning ally account and an internet connection. use the separate voiceover or talkback directions below. step-by-step instructions from learning ally’s official app page, follow the link for your device’s app store. confirm the application and developer before installing it, then open the app. follow the sign-in route your school or membership requires. pause to identify each field before typing, especially if a school service opens another sign-in screen. explore the bookshelf and locate the intended title. activate it and inspect its reading or download options. complete a download if you intend to read offline. open the book. navigate to the playback control by its spoken label and activate it. pause again before navigating chapter or study controls. use the app’s chapter, section, or page navigation to select a known passage. confirm it by its heading or opening words, then resume playback. before leaving the app, record your passage and check any bookmark or note you created. if you switch devices, connect both as needed and verify where the book opens. check your result you can use the mobile player through labeled controls and return to a known reading location. if something goes wrong if one tap only speaks a control instead of activating it, your mobile screen reader is doing its normal focus action; use its activation gesture below. if the app reports an access error, resolve the membership or login route rather than reinstalling repeatedly. try it yourself open a book, play a passage, pause it, change chapters, and return using a saved marker. documentation: official learning ally app choices · official android application . iphone and android: focus, activate, and enter text iphone or ipad with voiceover swipe right with one finger to the next item; swipe left to the previous item. a one-finger double-tap activates the selected item. at a text field, select it and double-tap to edit. with standard typing, select a keyboard key then double-tap; touch typing instead enters the selected key when you lift your finger. android with talkback swipe right or left with one finger to move focus. double-tap to activate. use two fingers to scroll. keyboard entry depends on the keyboard and typing settings; on gboard, locate a key by touch and lift to enter it. use this routine with the reading app before activating anything, hear its full label. the book title, a download control, and the play control perform different actions. activate once, wait, and identify the new screen. an app can open an account page or download details rather than immediately playing. during book narration, pause the player before exploring unfamiliar controls so their labels are easier to hear. if the expected item is missing, check whether a dialog, keyboard, or menu is still open. follow the device’s back or dismissal behavior and identify where you land. if voiceover or talkback is off, ordinary touch interaction applies: tap the labeled control to activate it. these touch directions do not define external-keyboard shortcuts. customized gestures may differ; use your device’s screen-reader help if the standard gesture does something else. documentation: apple voiceover operation , voiceover typing , talkback gestures , and talkback typing . continue with the full voiceover manual or talkback manual for device-level practice. check offline readiness and recover a missing passage start here: the installed reading app on the exact device you will use away from the internet. browser access alone is not proof of offline readiness. step-by-step instructions while connected, select the intended book and complete the app’s download procedure. check the status until it indicates completion; a title appearing on a shelf is not sufficient. open the downloaded book and read a short passage. note its title, edition, chapter, and page or section. at a convenient time when disconnecting will not interrupt another task, temporarily disconnect that device and test the same book. confirm that you can start playback and navigate to a second passage. reconnect afterward. if offline playback failed, check storage, download status, and app-specific help while connected. do not erase other people’s files to free space. when continuing elsewhere, open the same account and book edition, then compare the current passage with your written location. use navigation or a bookmark to recover if needed. before removing downloads or reinstalling an app, check whether important notes and progress are synchronized or recorded elsewhere. check your result you know whether this book on this device works offline and have a way to regain your place. if something goes wrong report the device, app/version, title, connection state, exact message, and last successful action. keep passwords and private account information out of support screenshots. try it yourself demonstrate offline reading for one downloaded title, reconnect, and return to your recorded passage. documentation: official reading-app guidance . keyboard and control reference keyboard access in a desktop reading environment purpose routine locate controls tab forward; shift+tab backward; listen to each label activate a focused button enter or space when supported start or pause audio focus the player’s labeled playback button before activating choose a chapter or page open the player’s navigation control and follow the available choices avoid competing voices pause the book while listening to control labels a bare space press is not guaranteed to play or pause in every context. it can affect the page or the currently focused control. on mobile, use your device’s screen-reader gestures instead of desktop keyboard assumptions. source: reading navigation features . independent practice choose any activity; there is no required order or passing score. identify your account’s correct login method. find and add the correct edition of a book. navigate to an assigned passage and explain its main point. use a bookmark to revisit a study question. complete an offline test in your installed app before a trip. after each task, record whether you completed it independently, needed a prompt, or want another attempt. repeat the difficult step instead of restarting everything. related learning compare the bookshare and bard mobile manuals. use the voiceover or talkback manual for mobile navigation. this manual now has ten dedicated lessons, a final quiz, and a printable course-completion certificate. lesson completion is self-reported. back to all manuals · back to the beginning practice this topic in mission control choose command practice or choose topic missions , then select learning ally. these are simulated exercises; they do not operate the actual app or account. topic missions presents a troubleshooting problem. command practice explains and checks one keyboard action at a time. use settings to choose speech and sound feedback. escape returns to the topic list during a session. when a simulator prompt says protected practice, release the modifier before the final key as instructed. in the real application, use the held keyboard combination in this manual. completing a simulation does not confirm that the real application received or performed a command. © 2026 accessible learning center

entries.text: accessible audio recording and editing manual skip to main content accessible media accessible audio recording and editing manual record, review, edit, save, and export audio in audacity. basic how-tos advanced how-tos command list first-time keyboard guide use this short routine before following the accessible audio recording and editing manual procedures. it explains exactly how the keyboard directions in this manual work. press a single key find the named key without pressing it if possible. press and release the key one time. do not hold it unless the step specifically says to hold it. stop and listen to the full screen-reader announcement before pressing another key. press a keyboard combination when a command contains a plus sign, such as ctrl+s, hold down the first key. while continuing to hold the first key, press and release the final key once. release the first key. the plus sign is not a key and should not be pressed. listen for the expected result described in the procedure. if nothing changes, verify that the correct application or webpage has focus and try the command once more. press a sequence of keys when keys are separated by commas or the word “then,” press and release them in order instead of holding them together. after each key, listen for a menu, tab, control, or new screen before continuing. if the announcement does not match the step, press escape once to close the current menu or dialog and restart that procedure. know which navigation key to try tab and shift+tab: move forward and backward among buttons, links, fields, and other controls. arrow keys: move inside menus, lists, groups of choices, text, and many screen-reader reading views. enter: opens the selected item or activates the focused command. space: activates many buttons and checks or clears checkboxes. in a text field, space ty

entries.text: microsoft edge screen reader manual skip to main content accessible learning center manual microsoft edge screen reader manual narrator, nvda, and jaws independent self-study guide for web browsing all manuals table of contents start of manual first-time keyboard guide use this short routine before following the microsoft edge screen reader manual procedures. it explains exactly how the keyboard directions in this manual work. press a single key find the named key without pressing it if possible. press and release the key one time. do not hold it unless the step specifically says to hold it. stop and listen to the full screen-reader announcement before pressing another key. press a keyboard combination when a command contains a plus sign, such as ctrl+s, hold down the first key. while continuing to hold the first key, press and release the final key once. release the first key. the plus sign is not a key and should not be pressed. listen for the expected result described in the procedure. if nothing changes, verify that the correct application or webpage has focus and try the command once more. press a sequence of keys when keys are separated by commas or the word “then,” press and release them in order instead of holding them together. after each key, listen for a menu, tab, control, or new screen before continuing. if the announcement does not match the step, press escape once to close the current menu or dialog and restart that procedure. know which navigation key to try tab and shift+tab: move forward and backward among buttons, links, fields, and other controls. arrow keys: move inside menus, lists, groups of choices, text, and many screen-reader reading views. enter: opens the selected item or activates the focused command. space: activates many buttons and checks or clears checkboxes. in a text fie

entries.text: accessible learning center accessible learning center free, step-by-step technology lessons for blind and low-vision learners. choose a starting point below. read the manuals and lessons without creating an account. start learning computer basics start with windows, keyboard navigation, files, and folders. screen readers get started with jaws, nvda, or windows narrator. workplace skills begin with word, then explore spreadsheets, email, and teamwork. google tools begin with chrome, then explore docs, drive, and gmail. braille technology start with focus 40 blue, or find a guide for another device . ai skills learn ai basics and responsible use before exploring individual tools. browse or find help all manuals all lessons search resources continue learning review progress enter student id quizzes and certificates how progress works choose a lesson, complete its activities using your preferred assistive technology, and mark it complete. use the same anonymous student id when you return to review saved progress. for instructors, families, and support groups share a direct link to a manual or lesson that matches a learner’s goal. the public materials are free to read and can support practice between teaching sessions. mission control — coming soon interactive command practice and troubleshooting missions are being tested. view the testing preview . © 2026 accessible learning center
